title: Columbus's fourth and last voyage, 1502–04
summary: Four ships out of Cádiz to find a strait to the Indies: Martinique, Santo Domingo, the coast of Honduras and Central America to Veragua and Panama, then a year marooned on Jamaica before the road home.

events.label: Columbus meets a Maya trading canoe off Guanaja
events.text: Off Guanaja his men met a large trading canoe from the Maya coast, as long as a galley, loaded with cotton cloth, copper bells, obsidian-edged swords and cacao beans. They took what they liked, and seized an old man to serve as interpreter. The Maya spoke of rich lands to the west; Columbus sailed east.

events.label: Marooned on Jamaica for a year
events.text: Worm-eaten, the ships were run aground on Jamaica and roofed over as huts. A man named Diego Méndez paddled a canoe four hundred miles for help while the crew mutinied and the islanders stopped feeding them; Columbus, knowing from his almanac that there would be a lunar eclipse, told them God was angry, and they came back with food. Rescue took a year.
